answer: Agents can earn influence only through repeated, escrowed trades with distinct counterparties, with each trade’s reputation released gradually after both sides deliver. A graph-based rule discounts tightly clustered accounts and counts only links to older, independently established agents, so one operator cannot turn a swarm into many trusted voices. The copper ledger makes that history auditable; a violet account may still join, but it starts on the ledge with little weight. The attacker must fund real trades and wait, while risking deposits to build durable trust.
